questions.q: Scenario: a leaderboard test covers the next 16 days. You use a random 80/20 split of rows for validation and get an excellent score, but the leaderboard score is poor. Why?
options: The random split leaks future information into training and does not copy the real task
why: Correct: use a time-based split with the same horizon.

questions.q: Scenario: the competition metric is RMSLE and sales have a long right tail. What do you do with the target?
options: Train on log1p(y) with MSE and invert with expm1
why: Correct: MSE on log1p(y) is exactly RMSLE.
Raw squared error is dominated by large values.
Large values are real and counted.
